question.knowledge_point: Identifying Intervals On Which the IVT Can Be Applied
question.problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x)$ is defined as

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}x+1, & x\le 1 \\ 5-2x, & x>1.\end{aligned}
$$

On which of the following intervals can the intermediate value theorem be applied to the function?
question.worked_solution:
The intermediate value theorem can be applied to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

The function is discontinuous at $x=1.$ To see this, we note that

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)=2\ne 3={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x).
$$

 

We conclude that the intermediate value theorem can be applied to the function $f(x)$ only on closed intervals that do not contain the point $x=1.$ 

From the given options, only the interval $[-2,0]$ is allowed.  The intervals $(1,3]$ and $[-2,1)$ are not closed, $[-2,1]$ and $[0,3]$ contain the point $x=1.$

evidence.solution_quote: From the given options, only the interval $[-2,0]$ is allowed.  The intervals $(1,3]$ and $[-2,1)$ are not closed, $[-2,1]$ and $[0,3]$ contain the point $x=1.$
